key_insight: ToroFit identifies toroidal components in high-dimensional point clouds and fits them with low-energy trigonometric models.
engineering_relevance: The framework provides nonlinear coordinates and fitted models that can support interpolation, denoising, and analysis of recurrent or quasiperiodic data.
method: Use persistent cohomology and cup products to identify distinct toroidal components.
Fit each component using low-energy multivariate trigonometric polynomials.
Reduce the fitting problem to generalized ridge regression.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports demonstrations on synthetic and real data, including recurrent-video interpolation, quasiperiodic attractor recovery, and parasite and human gene-space cycles.
watch_item: Applicability depends on whether the data lie near a wedge sum of tori; the abstract does not quantify robustness to noise or departures from this structure.
paper_title: ToroFit: Fitting Wedge Sums of Tori to High-Dimensional Data
